newsitem.title: CANADA: Rogers to sell units to Cogeco Cable.
newsitem.headline: Rogers to sell units to Cogeco Cable.

text.p: Rogers Communications Inc and Cogeco Cable Inc said on Wednesday they inked a deal under which Rogers will sell Cogeco Cable some of its Ontario cable systems for about C$1,180 per subscriber or total proceeds of roughly C$350 million.
The purchases will add 300,000 subscribers to Cogeco Cable's 455,000-subscriber base, bringing it up to 755,000.

Cogeco Cable will pay about C$300 million of the proceeds in cash upon closing, which is expected by November 15. One-third of the balance will be paid to Rogers in the form of subordinate voting shares, subject to stock exchange approvals.
The remaining two-thirds will be in the form of notes payable over the ensuing two years.
Rogers will continue to manage the systems pending approval of the deal by the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission, the companies said.

The Ontario systems in the sale serve Hamilton, Niagara Falls, St. Catharines, Sarnia, Wallaceburg, Peterborough, the Ottawa Valley, Cornwall and North Bay. Except for Cornwall and part of Hamilton, the cable systems were acquired as part of Rogers' takeover of Maclean Hunter Ltd in 1994.

"This transaction, together with the injection into the cable company of the proceeds from the sale of The Toronto Sun, will substantially improve the financial position of the cable group," said Rogers president and chief executive Ted Rogers in a statement.

"It will also allow us to focus our efforts more closely on the deployment of innovative new services to the 2.2 million cable subscriber homes that we will continue to serve in the clustered and fibre interconnected areas of Greater Toronto, the Guelph to London corridor, Ottawa, and the lower mainland of British Columbia," Rogers added."

Cogeco Cable president and chief executive Louis Audet said: "The purchase of these systems from Rogers will increase Cogeco Cable's subscriber base in Canada from 455,000 to 755,000, with large clusters serving over 430,000 cable subscribers in key urban areas of that province."
